messages.subject: Line transect data - how to deal with an abnormal detection
messages.subject_clean: Line transect data - how to deal with an abnormal detection
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have counted a single bird species in a given area, through 15 random lin=
e transects, monthly across a calendar year as part of my PhD research. Usi=
ng Distance, I then ran MCDS models with covariates like habitat and cluste=
r size and as part of results, I am getting a not-normal detection probabil=
ity where the detection probability is significantly less than 1 closer to =
the transect (0m perpendicular distance), close to 1 around 30m perpendicul=
ar distance from the transect and decreasing then onwards. I am wondering i=
f there is a way to deal with this abnormal detection probability? Any advi=
ce would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance,

Kasun

Kasun Ekanayake | Ph.D Candidate
School of Life and Environmental Sciences
Deakin University | Burwood, Victoria, Australia
Email - kbek...@deakin.edu.au

--

messages.subject: rescaling covariates in mcds
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am adding covariates to detection function models within mrds, and I've
just noticed that if I rescale numerical covariates so as to always fall
between 0 and 1 I can get models to fit successfully where previously they
fell over. I include a code excerpt below which illustrates this behaviour
for two numerical covariates (cluster size and body length).

So, from now on I will rescale all my covariates, but wondering if this
represents a bug in the code,  or if I'm failing to set some option which
would avoid this behaviour.

Best wishes

Nigel

messages.subject: Re: rescaling covariates in mcds
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nigel, list,

This is a known issue and does not necessarily represent a "bug", as
such. I have written some information about optimisation issues
(regarding my Distance package, but this extends to mrds too), which can
be found here:

https://github.com/dill/Distance/wiki/OptimisationIssues

I hope this helps!

best,
--dave
